The rendered product price is AllPrices.FirstOrDefault() and the resolver-context currencyCode is consumed ONLY for the empty-price fallback, so on a SINGLE-priced product the currency argument is structurally unobservable: one price row means FirstOrDefault() and a currency-aware selection return the same row, and in a second currency both fall to the same empty-price fallback. THE TWO AMOUNTS DIFFER ON PURPOSE. Every currency on this environment is registered at exchangeRate 1, so equal amounts would make a CONVERTING implementation indistinguishable from a correctly SELECTING one. If either fails, the discriminating arm is BLOCKED:PRECONDITION_UNMET and never PASS — a single-currency environment, or a fixture that has collapsed back to one price, makes the prices looking right indistinguishable from a currencyCode argument that changed nothing. Read the direction of this gate carefully: it is a gate on the FIXTURE and on the SELECTOR. A modal reading that fails to differ across the two sessions is a FAIL of this case, never a BLOCKED.

THE CELL THIS CASE EXISTS FOR IS culture x currency, NOT currency ALONE. Top-level mission money is formatted from CultureName by AfterMediatorSend while product money resolves off currencyCode, so the mismatch only becomes reachable when CULTURE is the thing that moves. Varying the session currency alone leaves CultureName pinned and compares two fields that both travel the AfterMediatorSend path — they agree by construction, and a green there says nothing about the mechanism. This case therefore runs TWO arms and reports them separately: ARM 1 varies the session currency at fixed culture and is scored on goal-denomination invariance, because a stored goal must not follow the session; ARM 2 varies the CULTURE at fixed session currency and compares a TOP-LEVEL money field against a PRODUCT money field, which is the only pair on this feature whose two members travel different formatting inputs.
ARM 2 needs a product money field and the order-value card has none. ARM 1 still reports its own verdict in that case. The Test Model cell names de-DE; where the store offers a different second locale that locale serves the same purpose, because the arm needs a culture CHANGE and not one specific culture.
DECIDABILITY GATE, ARM 1 — the store must offer at least one selectable session currency besides its default; where it does not, ARM 1 is BLOCKED:PRECONDITION_UNMET and ARM 2 still runs.
Where the card renders no goal target of its own, the goal reading is taken from the order-goal modal opened from that same card, and the case records which surface each of the two readings came from. A comparison built from one reading only is recorded NOT-DECIDABLE, never PASS.
DISPOSABLE FIXTURE, TERMINAL ONCE COMPLETED: mission progress is monotonic with no reset path, and a sibling suite placing real orders on these accounts can consume them between seed and execution. There is no @td() alias for the USER role today, so [PRE:SIGNIN_AS:USER] does not resolve either; the sign-in is therefore in Steps against {{USER_EMAIL}} / {{USER_PASSWORD}}, the env binding that resolves to the progress owner on every environment because the seeder resolves the same role the same way.
Store @td(MSN_STORE_SETTINGS.store_id) has @td(MSN_STORE_SETTINGS.setting_name)=true and @td(MSN_STORE_SETTINGS.base_setting_name)=true, and the loyalty missions fixture set is seeded.
DECIDABILITY, why this case is not vacuous — the completed bar variant renders only for a mission whose backend status is Completed, and on this identity the grid carries ONE OF EACH in a single pass: @td(MSN_PROGRESS_COMPLETED.name) is Completed at @td(MSN_PROGRESS_COMPLETED.progress_percentage) percent, and @td(MSN_PROGRESS_PARTIAL.name) is InProgress at @td(MSN_PROGRESS_PARTIAL.progress_percentage) percent. On an identity with no completed mission the variant never renders at all and the case is unfalsifiable, which is why it was deferred.
NO-HARDCODE, stated because it shapes the assertions: the success token's VALUE is deliberately never transcribed into this case (.claude/rules/test-data.md GOLDEN RULE — a transcribed colour is correct exactly once and then manufactures phantom failures, as the 14-value spacing grid did in REG-2026-07-24-2121). It is derived IN THE SAME PASS from another element on the SAME card that carries the same token: the 'Completed' success chip. scripts/lib/design-tokens.generated.ts carries spacing, breakpoints, control sizes and viewports but NO colour export, so a same-page derivation is the only hardcode-free oracle available today; adding a colour-token generator plus its tokens:check drift guard is recorded as a candidate rather than worked around with a literal.
The mission list spans several pages on the seeded store, so page to a named card rather than assuming page 1.
